title: HYDRAULIC STEERING-VALVES & HOSES
summary: Power steering (N40) control valve: the valve and adapter thread onto the end of the relay rod (center link) and are clamped with a bolt; the valve's own ball stud goes up through the pitman arm with a castle nut and cotter pin. Two steel pipes connect the valve to the power cylinder, and the pitman arm is held on the steering gear by the gear nut.

fastening.note: The valve's ball stud (part of [8], no separate callout) goes up through the end of the pitman arm [3]; castle nut [1] on top, locked with cotter pin [2].
Pitman arm [3] goes on the steering gear shaft and is held by the gear nut (marked as a production part, no callout).
Valve adapter [8] threads onto the end of the relay rod (gap .06 to .12) and is clamped by bolt [5] with lock washer [4] through the adapter clamp.
Pipes [6] and [7] run from the valve [8] fittings to the power cylinder ports; tube nuts at the valve torque 3. Keep pipe positions as shown to avoid twisting the hoses (see note).
View A: hose-valve outlet and hose-valve inlet fittings set at 17° and 45° from the valve centerline. View B: pipe angles 25°, 27°, 22°11' from vertical.

notes: NOTE Pipe positions shown must be maintained when assembling hoses to cylinder, to avoid twisting of hoses and possible interference with neighboring parts.
CAUTION While lubricating, rock pitman arm to break the seal at the seat and relieve pressure so grease can escape from the seal; otherwise the seal can rupture.
